_comment: Built-in text used when the Player2 AI is unavailable. {slot} words are filled from the lists of the same name. Keep it grounded and grim.

sign_state: the paint flaking away in long strips
one chain snapped so it hangs askew
newly repainted by someone with more will than skill
black with soot from a fire nobody talks about
building: A long, low building of wattle and daub, its thatch green with moss
A stone house that was a toll post once, its arrow slits stuffed with rags
A timber hall leaning against the old town wall
A sprawling inn with a stable yard ankle-deep in manure
A squat house of fieldstone, half sunk into the hillside
light: a single rushlight gutters on each table
the hearth gives more smoke than light
tallow candles throw a greasy yellow glow
grey daylight leaks through the shutters and shows every stain
smell: boiled mutton, with a whiff of the privy from the yard
sound: someone in the corner coughs and does not stop
a fiddler saws at a tune nobody asked for
the keeper's wife shouts at a boy in the kitchen
two drovers argue about the price of wool
crowd: a handful of drovers nurse their cups by the hearth
the tables are mostly empty, and the few drinkers keep their backs to the wall
a pair of soldiers in faded livery watch the door
farmhands crowd the benches, muddy to the knee
a pedlar sleeps sitting up, one hand on his pack
detail: A notice nailed by the door offers two silver for wolf ears.
Someone has carved a tally of forty-odd marks into the bar.
A dark stain on the floorboards has been scrubbed at and not quite removed.
Bundles of feverfew hang from the rafters to keep off sickness.
A rusted pike hangs over the hearth, notched along the blade.
The only window is patched with oiled parchment.
A dog with one ear sleeps under the stairs and growls at every new boot.
description: {building}. Inside, {light}, and the air is thick with {smell}. {crowd}; {sound}. {detail}
The door sticks and has to be shouldered open. Low beams, black with years of smoke, press close over a room that smells of {smell}. {crowd}. {detail}
{building}. The common room smells of {smell}, and {sound}. {crowd}. {detail}
manner: {keeper} looks every stranger up and down and asks for coin before pouring.
{keeper} is friendly enough, but never takes an eye off the door.
{keeper} says little, waters the ale and remembers every face.
{keeper} greets travellers loudly and overcharges them cheerfully.
{keeper} keeps a cudgel under the counter and has used it this week.
overheard: "Third one this month. River gave him back without his hands."
"Tax man came through again. Took the seed grain this time."
"Don't drink from the mill brook. My sister's boy did, and now he's shitting blood."
"If the lord wants soldiers, he can come and drag them off himself."
"Wolves were at the sheep again. Big ones. Bigger than wolves ought to be."
"Priest says the fever's a punishment. Punishment for what, I'd like to know."
region: rich farmland still scarred by last year's war

opening: Another day on the road: {miles} miles, {road}, through {lands}.
{miles} miles today, {road}. {lands}, and more of it.
walking: The weather was {weather}, and you felt every mile of it.
Under {weather}, the hours went by one step at a time.
{weather}: the kind of day you only notice when it is over.
Your boots knew the ground better than your eyes did by the end. {weather}.
closing: At the end of it: {mood}, and still walking.
